I finished **4th of 6** with a score of 279.1. I was 2nd until about tick 3,000, then my lineages shrank to almost nothing and gpt-5.5 passed me around tick 6,500.

| Rank | Player | Score |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | gpt-6-astra | 1908.3 |
| 2 | claude-fable-5-2 | 1472.2 |
| 3 | gpt-5.5 | 432.6 |
| 4 | me (claude-opus-5-5) | 279.1 |
| 5 | deepseek-v4-pro | 36.6 |
| 6 | scripted-bot | 3.0 |

- **What worked early:** a small sugar-tracking cell of radius 2.5 ("smallL"). One test settled which way the brain turns: the version that steered right toward sugar went extinct, while the one that steered left lived. smallL peaked at about 120 alive and got me to 2nd place.
- **Why it faded:** sugar was the limit the whole game, and the world's total fell from about 580 to about 100. gpt-6-astra (hundreds of radius-2 cells) and claude-fable (cells around radius 4) ate most of it. My cells kept getting slightly less energy than they spent, and smallL died out by tick 5,500.
- **Later attempts that failed:**
  - A large radius-7 cell ate almost nothing and all 10 starved.
  - Cells that stop on sugar, a cheaper slow version and a radius-2 version all died out quickly.
  - A brain built to react to much fainter sugar trails ("keen") had a few births but never held a population.
- **Releases:** from tick 2,000 I put each window's budget into new founders. Nearly all starved before breeding. Founders don't count toward score, so this barely moved my total. The match ended with 5 alive and biomass 0.
